title: Tokenizer hinting and batched ingest for low-latency prefill throughput
creator: Sofia Martinez
description:
Problem: Prefill-side overhead for multi-turn sessions and high- qps workloads is dominated by per-request tokenizer startup, unicode normalization, and allocation churn. This increases p50/p95 prefill latency and forces the runtime to pick less-efficient kernel schedules because sequence length distribution appears more variable.

Goal: Reduce prefill CPU overhead and tail latency by introducing lightweight tokenizer hinting, batched ingest for simultaneous requests from the same session or route, and a shared in-memory ingest buffer with pre-allocated allocations. Integrate hints with the kernel selection layer so kernel choice can assume more stable sequence length distribution and enable attention kernel optimizations for short/medium contexts.
acceptance_criteria: p50 prefill tokenization CPU time reduced by >= 40% on synthetic multi-tenant workload
p95 end-to-end prefill latency reduced by >= 20% for sessions with average prompt length < 512
No regression on semantic tokenization correctness across existing evaluation prompts
Kernel routing uses stable length bucket in >= 85% of batched sessions, demonstrated in runtime traces
Feature gated rollout and observability dashboard showing hit-rate of tokenizer hints and shared buffer reuse
design_notes: Introduce a small TokenizerHint object emitted by client SDKs / routing layer that contains: expected prompt length bucket, is_ascii_fastpath boolean, session_affinity_id optional string. Hints are advisory only and validated server-side.

Server-side ingest layer will maintain a short-lived batching window (~3-8ms) keyed by (route, model, session_affinity_id) to coalesce incoming prefill requests and run tokenization in a single worker invocation.
Shared ingest buffer: use a thread-local slab allocator with fixed-size chunks (configurable by model family) to avoid per-request Vec/String allocations during normalization and token assembly.

Unicode normalization path: add a heuristic early-exit for ASCII-only inputs and a vectorized chunked normalizer for common unicode sequences. Use a rapid ASCII-scan that also records whether characters are likely to produce long token sequences.

Kernel selection integration: the tokenization worker will emit a length_prediction tag with median and max predicted tokens for the batch. The scheduler consumes this to pick attention kernels and batching strategies (e.g., short-context kernel vs. long-context kernel).

Fall-back behavior: If any hint mismatches tokenized output significantly, mark the session's hint as invalidated and fallback to conservative kernel routing for a TTL period. Metrics capture mismatch counts.

Security and correctness: All hints are treated as untrusted; we validate lengths and never change semantics of tokenization. No user-visible changes to tokens; tests must pass existing tokenizer unit suite.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (Spike, 2d): Implement TokenizerHint proto and a router-side shim to attach session_affinity_id. Benchmark overhead of hint propagation across the RPC stack.
Phase 2 (Core, 6d): Implement batched ingest window keyed by (route, model, session_affinity_id) with single-worker tokenization and slab buffer allocator. Add ASCII early-exit path.
Phase 3 (Integration, 4d): Emit length_prediction tags to kernel selection; add scheduler logic to prefer short-context kernels for >80% confidence batches.
Phase 4 (QA/Rollout, 3d): Add golden dataset checks, fuzz tests for unicode correctness, and feature flag/remote-config for rollout.
Phase 5 (Observability, 2d): Dashboards: hint hit-rate, buffer reuse rate, tokenizer CPU time histogram, mismatch rate, kernel routing distribution.
Target PRs: one for ingestion layer change, one for tokenizer kernel optimizations, one for scheduler integration and metrics.
testing_plan: Unit tests: tokenizer equivalence tests across full Unicode plane and ASCII fastpath fuzzing
Performance tests: microbench harness with synthetic multi-session workload to measure tokenization CPU and latency
Integration tests: end-to-end against runtime with kernel selection to assert routing changes are applied
Canary: run under dedicated capacity with low-percentage traffic, monitor mismatch and latency metrics for 48 hours
rollout_plan: Feature gate controlled by runtime flag 'tokenizer_hint_batched_ingest' default off
Enable for internal staging and dedicated test cluster 1 -> 10% production traffic -> 50% -> 100% with 24h observation windows
If mismatch_rate > 0.5% or 10% regression in p95, rollback immediately and collect traces
Post-rollout, enable automated TTL tuning based on buffer reuse signals
risks: Risk: Hints could be abused or mismatched causing suboptimal kernel selection. Mitigation: server-side validation and TTL invalidate policy.
Risk: Batching window increases serialization latency for single-request flows. Mitigation: keep window small (3-8ms) and only batch when session_affinity_id present or route high-qps.
Risk: Shared slab allocator introduces memory fragmentation in long-lived processes. Mitigation: thread-local slabs with periodic reclamation and telemetry to detect leaks.
Risk: Unicode vectorized normalizer introduces subtle tokenization divergences. Mitigation: strict unit test coverage and fall back to scalar normalizer on mismatch detection.
